summary: The patch changes SSTable.delete() in src/java/org/apache/cassandra/io/sstable/SSTable.java so it reads each component's lastModified once, sorts the components ascending, and deletes in that order. This is so a crash partway through deletion leaves the newest file, and so the REMOVE-record timestamp, intact. The diff has no test changes at all. The JIRA test plan says 'additions to LogTransactionTest', but none are in the patch. Checklist applied: the cassandra-injvm-dtest SKILL.md from the bundle, plus testing_doc. The dtest guide does not call for a multi-node test here, because this is single-node file-deletion logic where a unit test in test/unit is the right suite. Not reviewed: nothing. The tier is small and the whole diff was read.

findings.rule: Bug fix needs a regression test that fails without the fix; the ticket's own test plan promises LogTransactionTest additions
findings.problem: The patch fixes a crash-recovery bug (a node fails to start with a 'corrupted' txn log after a partial SSTable delete) but adds or changes no test file. Nothing checks that SSTable.delete() removes files in ascending lastModified order. Nothing checks that, after deleting only a prefix of the files, the max lastModified of the survivors still equals the REMOVE record. If someone reverts to the old 'DATA first, SUMMARY last' order, or edits the sort comparator, no test fails. The LogTransactionTest additions named in the JIRA test plan are absent, so the patch does not meet its own plan.
findings.fix: Add a unit test in test/unit/org/apache/cassandra/db/lifecycle/LogTransactionTest.java. Create an SSTable's component files with strictly increasing lastModified values, giving the DATA file a timestamp that is not the oldest. Call SSTable.delete, or the tidier, with a hook that stops partway, or assert the delete order. Then assert that LogFile.verifyRecord on the REMOVE record still passes on the partial state. The test must fail against the base code, where DATA is deleted first.

findings.rule: Coverage of boundaries and error paths
findings.problem: The new code has branches that are not exercised: components with equal lastModified values (coarse filesystem timestamp granularity, where the stable sort falls back to Set iteration order), and a component whose file is already missing (File.lastModified() returns 0, so it sorts first). Delete also changed from FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm to FileUtils.delete for all components, which affects error handling for DATA and the other files. No test pins the new behaviour for ties, missing files or delete failures.
findings.fix: In the same LogTransactionTest additions, cover equal timestamps and an already-missing component. Assert the intended failure behaviour, or note in the PR why FileUtils.delete is acceptable in place of deleteWithConfirm.
